programme.title: The Elephant Man
programme.desc: Based on the life of John Merrick, a man born with a disfiguring disease who seemed doomed to a grim existence as a sideshow freak until taken in by a London surgeon and introduced to society. Despite his dreadful experiences, Merrick is a gentle, intelligent soul and becomes a popular guest in Victorian drawing rooms - but only if his deformed features are completely covered.

programme.title: Q.E.D.
programme.sub-title: The True Story of the Elephant Man
programme.desc: Using exclusive access to Joseph Merrick's case history and medical notes, this programme traces the story of the so-called Elephant Man's life, from his birth in Leicester to his premature death in the London Hospital.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: A look back at the life and work of Sir John Hurt, who died aged 77, after a career that spanned six decades and took in over 100 films. In a selection of rarely-seen interviews, we find John discussing some of his most iconic screen creations.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: An investigation into the appeal and power of the popular song `My Way', which was written by Paul Anka and recorded by artists including Frank Sinatra, Shirley Bassey, Elvis Presley and Sid Vicious.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: The multiple Grammy Award-winning singer joins a full orchestra for this one-off gig at the Royal Albert Hall, with incredible new arrangements of some of her most-loved songs. St Vincent is musician Annie Clark, whose artistry is in full hypnotic flow in this one-off spectacular. Conductor and arranger Jules Buckley brings the full might of his 60-strong orchestra to revel in other-wordly new arrangements of songs from seven St Vincent albums.

programme.title: Roxy Music and Bryan Ferry at the BBC
programme.desc: Enjoy the `Thrill of It All' and `Dance Away the Evening' for this dive into the BBC's archives to look over some of the finest performances from both Roxy Music and Bryan Ferry. As a band, they were innovative, helping create the look and sound of the 1970s, and Ferry's solo career saw him hit new heights as the embodiment of sophisticated cool. Amongst the hits included are classics like `Do The Strand', `Avalon', `Slave to Love' and `In Every Dream Home a Heartache'.

programme.title: The BBC One Sessions
programme.desc: Bryan Ferry is in concert at LSO St Luke's in Shoreditch, performing classic Roxy Music tunes plus solo tracks from his back catalogue, including `Let's Stick Together', `Avalon' and `More Than This'. He also debuts tracks from his album of Bob Dylan covers, `Dylanesque', his interpretation of songs such as `Simple Twist of Fate', `Positively 4th Street' and `Just Like Tom Thumb's Blues'.

programme.title: Roxy Music: A Musical History
programme.desc: A look at the music of rock band Roxy Music, who have a good claim to be one of the UK's most influential bands. Led by charismatic front man Bryan Ferry, their striking style and great songs won them an army of fans who would go on to make their own mark in the world of music.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: The story of a giant otter cub, who was rescued and is being raised by Brazilian naturalist Carolina Vargas. Sancho has to be bottle-fed, shown how to catch fish, and taught to outsmart the many predators of the Pantanal, the world's biggest wetland.

programme.title: The Yorkshire Dales
programme.desc: Adventurer and explorer Paul Rose starts his journey in the town of Hawes where locals now run many of their own services, including the buses. Paul checks out why cycling is so popular in the Dales and tries to get to the top of the Buttertubs Pass.

programme.title: The Cult of ...
programme.desc: Unearthing the history and anecdotes behind cult Sunday night dramas looks at `All Creatures Great and Small'. With its mix of stunning countryside, eccentric characters and romance, the show formed a template for Sunday night television. Interviewees including Christopher Timothy, Peter Davison, Robert Hardy, Carol Drinkwater, Lynda Bellingham, John McGlynn, producer Bill Sellars and writer Johnny Byrne reveal the struggles behind the success.

programme.title: Christopher Timothy and Peter Davison Remember All Creatures Great and Small
programme.desc: `All Creatures Great and Small,' a classic British TV drama, ran for seven series from 1978. Peter Davison and Christopher Timothy recall meeting the real James Herriot, and the original Siegfried and Tristan Farnon.

programme.title: All Creatures Great & Small
programme.desc: Calum welcomes the new arrivals - one that bites and one that fits Siegfried's domestic requirement. James, meanwhile, receives an invitation to examine Lord Buttermere's new stallion.

programme.title: All Creatures Great & Small

programme.title: Walking With..
programme.desc: Comic Jim Moir explores a fascinating corner of the Kent coast as he walks down to Dungeness. Along the way he meets locals, explores military ruins and rides a steam train.

programme.title: Around the World in 80 Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don is in South America, a continent twice the size of Europe and the home of more than 50,000 endemic plant species. In Rio de Janeiro, Monty visits the private garden of Brazil's most famous artist, Burle Marx. He views the ingenious floating gardens of the Amazon, and visits a crumbling estancia (ranch) in the windy Pampas. He ends his journey on the Pacific coast of Chile.

programme.title: Oak Tree: Nature's Greatest Survivor
programme.desc: George McGavin investigates the dramatic life of the oak tree, a species that makes extraordinary transformations as it meets the challenges of the four seasons.

programme.title: Banned! The Mary Whitehouse Story
programme.desc: A look back at Mary Whitehouse's campaigns, from her attacks on the BBC and boycotts against films like `Last Tango in Paris' to conflicts with feminists and the gay liberation movement, and her contention that pornography, made mainly by men for men, was not going to lead to greater happiness for society.

programme.title: Banned! The Mary Whitehouse Story
programme.desc: In the 1970s, Mary's battle with permissive society is hotting up, as suggestions that nothing should be censored gain currency. Nude actress Fiona Richmond publicly objects to Mary's `bullying' desire to stand in the way of her personal freedoms.

programme.title: Genius of the Ancient World
programme.desc: Bettany Hughes travels to China on the trail of Confucius, a great sage of Chinese history whose ideas have fundamentally shaped the country of his birth for around 2,500 years.

When the villainous snow leopard Tai Lung threatens Po's homeland, the hapless panda is chosen to fulfil an ancient prophecy and defend the Valley from attack. Training under Master Shifu, Po embarks on an epic high-kicking adventure as he sets out to thwart Tai Lung's evil plans. A DreamWorks animation.

programme.title: Kung Fu Panda 2
programme.desc: A panda must unlock the secrets of his past in order to defeat a formidable villain who plans to wipe out kung fu and conquer China.

programme.title: Kung Fu Panda 3
programme.desc: After reuniting with his long-lost father, Po must train a village of clumsy pandas to help him defeat a supernatural warrior who becomes stronger with each battle.

programme.title: Kung Fu Panda 4
programme.desc: When a powerful shape-shifting sorceress sets her eyes on Po's Staff of Wisdom, he suddenly realises he's going to need some help. Teaming up with a quick-witted corsac fox, he soon discovers that heroes can be found in the most unexpected places.
